tei:div.tei:p: This is the Aramaic source of Leah Horowitz’s teḥinah imahot, a teḥinah for Shabbat Mevorkhim, also known in its Yiddish translation (also by Leah Horowitz) as the “Teḥinah fun Sarah, Rivqah, Raḥel, vəLéah” as found in the manuscript: National Library of Israel (NLI), R41A460, vol. 6, no. 2.

The English translation was provided by Dr. Moshe Rosman as published in “Leah Horowitz’s Tkhine Imohos A Proto-Feminist Demand to Increase Jewish Women’s Religious Capital,” Polin 33 (2020), pp. 27-29, with minor amendments. (There, Rosman refers to the Aramaic form of the teḥinah as a piyyut.) I have parsed the Aramaic text and set each phrase side-by-side with its English translation. I have re-Hebraized names and divine names and omitted Rosman’s descriptive section titles. I have also changed Rosman’s translation from “supreme father and mother” to “supernal father and mother” in order to make the reference to the sefirot of Ḥokhmah and Binah clear in the translation.

The annotation is copied directly from Dr. Rosman’s footnotes. For the original footnote numbers, as well as a full analysis of the tekhinah in Aramaic, its Yiddish translation, and its Hebrew introduction, please consult the original article. –Aharon Varady
